title: Restore a qualified supervisor certificate
summary: Learn how to restore an expired qualified supervisor certificate at a Service NSW Centre or by post.
intro:
If your qualified supervisor certificate has expired, you can apply to restore the certificate within 3 months of expiry. You can do this at a Service NSW Centre or submit your renewal restoration notice by post.

If you do not apply for a restoration within 3 months, you'll need to apply for a new certificate. You cannot trade until the new certificate is issued.
who_can_apply: Your qualified supervisor certificate has expired.
what_you_need: Completed renewal restoration notice (or apply at a service centre if you do not have it)

external_links.text: Building, trade and specialist licences and registrations – Building Commission NSW

internal_links.text: Add your digital qualified supervisor certificate to the Service NSW app

faqs.q: How long do I have to restore my expired certificate?
faqs.a: You can apply to restore your certificate within 3 months of its expiry date.

faqs.q: What happens if I wait longer than 3 months to restore my certificate?
faqs.a: If you do not apply for a restoration within 3 months, you will need to apply for a new certificate. You cannot trade until the new certificate is issued.

faqs.q: What do I need to restore my certificate?
faqs.a: You need your proof of identity and your completed renewal restoration notice. If you do not have the notice, you can still apply at a service centre.
